articles.abstract: Turkish authorities have stepped up restrictions on hundreds of associations and medical organisations providing care to LGBTQI+ patients, the nation’s doctors have warned.1The Turkish Medical Association, the largest trade union representing medical doctors in Turkey, said that authorities began a wave of action after the government launched its national My Family is Safe campaign on 12 September.Officials claimed the initiative was needed to protect children and family values from influences on their sexual orientation and gender identity.It forms part of the Turkish government’s wider Decade of Family and Population programme, aimed in part at tackling the country’s falling birth rate.My Family is Safe has so far seen more than 400 websites and social media accounts, including those belonging to LGBTQI+ rights groups, activists, and health organisations, blocked or restricted.Among those affected are the Sexual Education, Treatment, and Research Association, whose account was withheld on X, and the Psychiatric Association of...

articles.title: 4D confocal microscopy of time dependent cell and nuclear osmotic response reveals differential osmoregulation and transport kinetics
articles.abstract: A cell's ability to maintain its volume is a prerequisite for its essential physiological functions. Changes in extracellular osmolarity induce the flux of water and solutes across the cell and nuclear membrane and, therefore, alters cell and nuclear volumes. Here, we investigated the equilibrium and dynamic volumetric responses of cells and nuclei in adherent human hepatoma (HepG2) cell monolayers using live three-dimensional imaging. Through image segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and volume rendering, precise cell and nuclear volumes were quantified. We found that during hypoosmotic stress, cells swell and lose osmolytes through active volume regulation, and nuclei undergo greater relative expansion than cells. During hyperosmotic stress, we found that both cells and nuclei shrink rapidly, develop irregular morphologies and undergo passive volume regulation. Furthermore, we explored the osmotic responses in these cells by restoring isosmotic conditions following osmotic stress and found that nuclei returned to volumes greater than their initial isosmotic volume, whereas cytoplasmic volume returned to a value below its initial isosmotic volume following swelling. By fitting coupled transport models water and solute permeability estimates for both cells and nuclei were made from their dynamic responses to different anisosmotic media with and without the presence of permeating solutes dimethyl sulfoxide and ethylene glycol. Together, these quantitative measurements of cell, cytoplasm, and nuclear volumetric responses and associated transport parameters have important implications for understanding cell physiology and the mechanism of osmoregulation.

articles.title: A comprehensive physiological dataset of pain and aversive modalities for pain biomarkers research
articles.abstract: While progress has been made in identifying pain biomarkers using neuroimaging, the development of reliable EEG-based biomarkers remains challenging, limited by small sample sizes and the lack of adequate control conditions. We present a comprehensive dataset from 125 pain-free adults, comprising electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings, and behavioural, sociodemographic, and psychological data. Galvanic skin response and electrocardiogram data were also recorded in a subset of participants (n = 76). Participants received two sustained painful stimulations (thermal, chemical) and two sustained aversive non-painful stimulations (auditory, taste), each delivered twice (with and without continuous intensity ratings). Data are provided in Brain Imaging Data Structure format, where all physiological, stimulus-related, and behavioural data are synchronized within the EEG data files for easy access and analysis. Technical validation confirmed data integrity, with spectral and physiological analyses showing responses associated with stimulus intensity and subjective pain/unpleasantness levels. By providing multimodal physiological data across painful and non-painful aversive conditions, this initiative represents a valuable resource for developing or validating biomarkers and exploring the multidimensional nature of pain perception.

articles.title: A map of RBP-miRNA regulatory connections for deciphering the mechanisms of transcriptome remodeling in cancer
articles.abstract: Micro-RNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression that influence cancer progression and outcome. Whereas transcriptional dysregulation of miRNA abundance underlies abnormal functionality of some miRNAs in cancer, emerging data points to RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) as prominent post-transcriptional regulators of miRNA activity. Here, by modelling the regulon activities of well-characterized miRNA families in RNA-seq data of a comprehensive collection of RBP inhibition experiments, human cell lines and tissues, we report a map of regulatory connections between 34 RBPs and 28 miRNAs. Furthermore, through a global analysis of the abundance as well as the activity of miRNAs in thousands of tumor and control samples from 17 human cancers, we show that RBP-driven regulation of miRNA activity is common in tumors and contributes to the heterogeneity in miRNA activity profiles. We uncover a set of RBPs that regulate the activity of tumor-suppressor and oncogenic miRNAs, including miR-29-3p, miR-17-5p and miR-19-3p. Of particular interest, we describe a pan-cancer negative regulatory role for DDX55 on the activity of the miR-29-3p family, a critical miRNA family with tumor suppressor functions that is involved in most human cancers. Our functional studies confirm that DDX55 inhibition restores the gene-silencing activity of miR-29-3p and reduces cancer cell viability. Overall, our study provides the first pan-cancer investigation of functional regulatory connections between RBPs and miRNAs, and highlights RBPs whose interventional modulation may serve as a new approach to reprogram abnormal miRNA activities in cancer.

articles.title: ASTRA enables zero-shot super-resolution of spatial transcriptomics across capture geometries
articles.abstract: Spatial transcriptomic super-resolution recovers tissue organization obscured by coarse sampling, but fitting a model to each section greatly increases computational cost and reduces practicality. We introduce ASTRA, a cross-platform pretrained model that reconstructs expression from histology and measured RNA by zero-shot inference. Training with arbitrarily shaped count-bearing regions, termed parents, enables one frozen model to accommodate dense bins and separated spots. Across six held-out Visium HD sections, ASTRA achieved higher correlations under dense-bin and pseudo-Visium sampling, lower dense-bin errors and substantially shorter processing times than existing methods. It improved colorectal tissue segmentation and tumor-boundary recovery. In real colorectal Visium, reconstruction spatially resolved a stromal transcriptional state supported by measured RNA. The same checkpoint supported regional and nucleus-associated analyses across 43 invasive lobular carcinoma sections and within-spot interpretation across 92 triple-negative breast cancer sections. ASTRA establishes a reusable framework for practical, cohort-scale spatial transcriptomic super-resolution across platforms.

articles.title: Activation thresholds set the speed of biochemical trigger waves
articles.abstract: Trigger waves are positive feedback-mediated traveling waves that propagate without slowing down or diminishing in amplitude, enabling biochemical coordination over distances where diffusion alone would be insufficient. Apoptosis can spread as trigger waves of caspase activity, as demonstrated in Xenopus eggs and egg extracts. We measured apoptotic wave speeds in extracts at two cell cycle states and found that waves propagated more slowly in M-phase arrested cytostatic factor (CSF) extracts than in interphase extracts (21 versus 27 m min-1). Luther's equation, v=2{surd}D{kappa}, predicts wave speed from the diffusion coefficient D and the positive-feedback doubling rate {kappa}. However, D and {kappa} were comparable between the two extracts and could not explain the speed difference. This discrepancy highlighted a key limitation of the classical equation: it does not account for an activation threshold in trigger wave initiation, and in fact the threshold required to trigger apoptosis was found to differ between cell cycle states. We therefore extended Luther's equation to include such a threshold, obtaining v{propto}{surd}(AD/Uc ), where A is the reaction rate and Uc is the activation threshold. Perturbing apoptotic sensitivity confirmed the predicted threshold-speed relationship. These findings establish the activation threshold as a key determinant of trigger wave speed and provide a broadly applicable scaling law for predicting the spread of switch-like biochemical signals.

articles.title: Are carbohydrate ring distortions determined by biology or crystallography? The impact of experimental conditions on structural data
articles.abstract: Carbohydrates are essential molecules involved in a wide range of biological processes. While their structural representation in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) has been hindered due to their highly diverse and flexible nature, advancements on X-ray crystallography and CryoEM are accelerating the obtaining of their experimental structures, which in turn supports improved analyses of their structural properties, such as the role of their non-chair conformations on biological processes. In this context, the current work provides a comprehensive and up to date overview of carbohydrate structures within the PDB through classification, quantification, and characterization of monosaccharides and glycan chains, incorporating Cremer-Pople puckering coordinates to evaluate pyranose conformations. Our findings show that, even with a steep increase in CryoEM structures including more complex oligosaccharides, carbohydrate data remains concentrate dinsmallglycanchains, with a about 4% of non-chair conformation sintopresolution structures. Free energy landscapes for the pyranose ring in the presence and absence of nine different binding proteins, including both enzymes and non-enzymes, reinforce the preferred stability of chairs and the rarity of conformational induction upon binding.

articles.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism
articles.abstract: Axons of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons "die back" in Parkinson's disease (PD), exhibiting early degeneration relative to cell bodies, a key feature also observed in PD models. A critical step towards understanding the process of axonal neurodegeneration is to determine the physiological properties of dopaminergic axons that are altered during the early stages of cellular dysfunction. Here, we compared the electrophysiology and calcium dynamics of dopaminergic axons in the MitoPark model of PD with age-matched controls. Our experiments show a pronounced reduction in action potential (AP)-evoked calcium signals in MitoPark axons that emerges well before the onset of dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. In addition, calcium imaging and direct axon recording revealed deficits in AP propagation accompanied by alterations in the axonal AP waveform. Therefore, our experimental findings identify the progression of axon-specific physiological deficits that occur long before neurodegeneration, more precisely defining the period that precedes axonal loss.

articles.title: Bone Marrow-Derived Cells Fuse with Bergmann Glia in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis
articles.abstract: Bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs) can infiltrate the brain and adopt new identities through transdifferentiation or fusion, yet their interactions with specific neural cells remain poorly defined. We examined BMDC fusion with Bergmann glia (BG), a key cerebellar support cell, in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis. After bone marrow transplantation, BMDCs fused with BG to form heterokaryons, retaining BG morphology and molecular markers. These heterokaryons contained donor and host nuclei that differed in both morphology and transcriptional activity. Remarkably, the BMDC nucleus localized not only to the soma but also along BG processes. This discovery identifies BMDC-BG fusion as a previously unrecognized form of glial plasticity, opening avenues for therapeutic strategies aimed at potentiating glial-mediated repair.

articles.title: Cholera toxin remodels intestinal immunity and suppresses systemic metabolism
articles.abstract: Cholera toxin (CTx) is a potent enterotoxin and widely used mucosal adjuvant, yet the acute host response to CTx itself, in the absence of a co-administered antigen, remains vague. In this study, we integrated physiological and metabolic phenotyping with intestinal transcriptomics, epithelial imaging, immune profiling, hepatic gene-expression analysis, and paired microbiome profiling to characterize the response to a single oral CTx exposure in mice. Within 24 h, CTx remodeled immune-cell composition in both epithelial and lamina propria compartments, with responses shaped by sex and genetic background. Recurrent changes included increased epithelial group 3 innate lymphoid cells, reduced lamina propria RORγt+ regulatory T cells, and decreased epithelial ILC1/NK cells in males of both strains. CTx also increased villus DCLK1+ tuft cells and reduced MUC2 immunoreactivity. Jejunal transcriptomics revealed induction of inflammatory defense, glycolytic, autophagy, and lipid-utilization programs together with suppression of proliferative and mitochondrial programs, consistent with coordinated stress adaptation. These local changes were accompanied by rapid restructuring of the fecal microbial community and by systemic hypometabolism, despite markedly different hypothermic responses across strains. CTx also elicited a selective hepatic stress and metabolic program, including conserved suppression of Cyp7a1 across sexes and strains. Together, these findings show that CTx alone rapidly reorganizes the intestinal immune, epithelial, metabolic, and microbial environment while suppressing whole-body metabolism. This work provides an integrated framework for understanding the acute host response to CTx and for interpreting its widespread use as a mucosal adjuvant. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Food Allergy Science Initiative, 2022-FASI-0001, 2023-FASI-AS23310 Hypothesis Fund, G11391-300 National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, https://ror.org/00adh9b73, R01DK143944 Arizona Department of Health Services, RFGA2024-022-020

articles.title: Closed-head injury produces a delayed, region-specific defect in glucose-carbon routing at the pyruvate branchpoint in APP/PS1 KI mice
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), and both conditions are associated with impaired glucose metabolism and mitochondrial dysfunction. We previously reported time-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction following closed-head injury (CHI) in amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) knock-in (KI) mice, but whether glucose-derived carbon labeling showed a corresponding temporal pattern remained unknown. We hypothesized that early deficits would involve tricarboxylic acid (TCA)-cycle metabolites, whereas chronic changes persisted upstream at the pyruvate-lactate branchpoint. Here, oral uniformly 13C-labeled glucose ([U-13C]-glucose) tracing and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS)-based isotopologue analysis were used to quantify first-turn glucose-derived carbon fate in cortex and hippocampus. To distinguish the effects of age at injury from those of post-injury interval, mice were analyzed 1 month after injury either at 7 or 12 months of age or 8 months after injury at 12 months of age. The most pronounced alterations occurred 8 months after CHI, when KI mice exhibited increased pyruvate and lactate labeling in the cortex and broader increases in glycolytic labeling in the hippocampus. These findings suggest that in APP/PS1 KI mice, chronic closed-head injury produced a delayed shift in glucose-derived carbon labeling centered on glycolytic and pyruvate/lactate nodes, with loss of hippocampal precursor-product coupling but without broad reduction of first-turn TCA-linked labeling.

articles.title: Combined celecoxib and NDGA induces a non-canonical, autophagy-independent redox cell death via p62/KEAP1 in colorectal cancer
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits substantial intratumoral heterogeneity, with differences in oncogenic driver mutations and apoptotic competence contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here, we investigated whether combined celecoxib and NDGA treatment (C+N) induces redox-mediated cell death via the p62/KEAP1 axis, offering a therapeutic approach that can overcome genetic diversity in CRC. We used two genetically distinct CRC cell lines, HCT116 and HT29, harbouring KRAS and BRAF mutations respectively, with differing p53 status, as models of tumor heterogeneity. C+N exhibited profound cytotoxicity in both cell lines, independent of COX-2/5-LOX expression and apoptotic competence. Additionally, C+N induced marked oxidative stress with mitochondrial ROS, lipid peroxidation, and labile ferrous iron accumulation, visualized as distinct JC-1 green mitochondrial puncta and FerroOrange red iron puncta in both cell lines. The antioxidant NAC reversed C+N-induced death, but inhibitors of apoptosis, autophagy, necroptosis, or ferroptosis did not, indicating a mechanism distinct from these pathways. Mechanistically, the combination induced p62 Ser349 phosphorylation, promoting KEAP1 degradation and NRF2 stabilization independently of ULK1-mediated autophagy; however, NRF2 stabilization was uncoupled from HO-1 induction. Our work reveals that C+N induces a ULK1/autophagy-independent, redox-mediated cell death mechanism that circumvents apoptotic competence, highlighting redox disruption as a genotype-independent therapeutic strategy to overcome CRC heterogeneity.

articles.title: Coordinated microRNA-mRNA regulatory remodelling across the compressed maturation of the African killifish (Nothobranchius furzeri)
articles.abstract: The turquoise killifish (Nothobranchius furzeri) is an emerging vertebrate model for development and ageing due to its exceptionally rapid maturation and short lifespan. However, how microRNA (miRNA) regulation coordinates gene expression across its compressed developmental trajectory remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated miRNA and mRNA expression from the same unexposed animals across three developmental stages: newly hatched fry (4 weeks total age), juveniles (~8 weeks total age), and aged adults (~8 months of age). Developmental stage was the dominant source of variation in both datasets, with miRNA and mRNA profiles independently resolving a consistent progression from newly hatched fry to juveniles and adults. Transcriptomic changes reflected ongoing tissue maturation, including increased expression of crystallin genes associated with lens development, while more than 2,000 genes were differentially expressed during the juvenile transition. Integration of 398 developmentally dynamic miRNAs with predicted mRNA targets identified specific miRNAs whose developmental changes were significantly enriched for opposing changes in their target genes. These included conserved developmental regulators from the miR-200/141, miR-29, let-7, and miR-34 families, which increased toward adulthood as their predicted target cohorts decreased. Stage-controlled analyses further identified miR-34a, miR-29a, miR-29b, miR-15a, and a novel candidate whose target relationships persisted independently of the overall developmental trajectory. Notably, miR-29 showed particularly strong induction during maturation, consistent with its conserved roles in extracellular-matrix remodeling, differentiation, and vertebrate ageing. Together, these findings reveal coordinated remodeling of conserved miRNA-mRNA regulatory programs across the rapid maturation of N. furzeri and establish a framework for investigating post-transcriptional regulation during vertebrate development in a species with limited miRNA annotation.

articles.title: Cross-Dataset Reanalysis of Mouse Alzheimer Disease Single-Cell RNA-Sequencing Data Reveals a Reproducible Innate Immune Activation Signature
articles.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies of Alzheimer disease (AD) mouse models have proliferated across independent laboratories, brain regions, and platforms, yet the cross-study reproducibility of transcriptional signatures derived from such data remains underexplored. We reanalyzed six publicly available mouse brain scRNA-seq datasets (GSE140399, GSE140510, GSE143758, GSE208683, GSE214244, and GSE296027; 360,620 cells, 102 annotated clusters) using a standardized pipeline (Figure 1) comprising quality control, Leiden clustering, confidence-tiered marker-based cell-type annotation, sample-level pseudobulk differential expression, cross-dataset consistency analysis, and pathway enrichment. Pseudobulk differential expression, performed on 32 samples (16 AD, 16 Control) from five of the six datasets, identified 301 significant genes (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05) out of 20,629 tested, of which 290 (96.3%) were upregulated and 11 (3.7%) downregulated in AD. The upregulated set was dominated by innate immune and interferon-response genes (Ccl3, Ccl4, Ccl6, Itgax, Cst7, Tlr4, Trem2) and showed extremely strong enrichment for immune system and innate immune system pathways (Reactome, p {equiv} 1.9 x 10-43 and 2.1 x 10-29 respectively), phagosome and osteoclast differentiation (KEGG), and interferon alpha/beta signaling. Of the 301 significant genes, 235 (78%) showed the same direction of effect across all datasets in which they were tested. The sixth dataset, GSE296027, was excluded from differential expression analysis due to a gene-identifier corruption artifact introduced during pseudobulk aggregation (detailed in Methods and Limitations) but contributed valid cell-type composition and microglial subclustering data, independently recovering a disease-associated microglia-like state. These findings indicate that a reproducible, strongly immune/interferon-skewed transcriptional signature, rather than a balanced up/down transcriptional shift, characterizes the mouse AD models analyzed here.

articles.title: Danuglipron and orforglipron engage GLP-1R through materially different interfaces: an unbiased molecular dynamics study
articles.abstract: GLP-1R is among the most heavily pursued targets in metabolic disease, but its natural agonist is a 30-residue peptide that must be injected. Two oral non-peptide agonists have reached late-stage trials. Cryo-EM studies have already shown that danuglipron and CHU-128, a close analogue of orforglipron, occupy the receptor differently, but not how either interface behaves over time. We ran 500 ns of unbiased all-atom molecular dynamics on GLP-1R bound to GLP-1, danuglipron (PF-06882961) and orforglipron (LY3502970), one trajectory each, in a POPC bilayer with the G protein removed. Although CHU-128 has been simulated before, its analogue, orforglipron, has not. Scored against contacts computed from the deposited structures, under a force field that shares no parameters with previous oral agonist studies, we recovered 80%, 86% and 79% above 50% occupancy. Indexing contact by chemical group, rather than by receptor residue, and normalising by molecular size, separates the two oral compounds: orforglipron carries ring systems dedicated almost entirely to one receptor domain, one of them directing 99.7% of its contact to the extracellular domain, whereas every group of danuglipron engages both. Danuglipron is correspondingly the outlier on measures that do not depend on a chosen threshold: only 33% of its contacts exceed 90% occupancy against 72% and 84%, and it is the only system whose occupancies remain unconverged at 100 ns. With single trajectories, these are observations rather than tested claims, but two drugs of the same class and comparable size occupy this receptor in structurally distinct ways.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Meets-Active Surfaces: A Unified Framework for Multi-Object Segmentation and Shape Analysis in 3D Fluorescence Microscopy
articles.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Nagini3D, a 3D biological image segmentation method that hybridizes two high-performing yet highly complementary segmentation paradigms: deep learning-based approaches and snake-based methods. Our approach leverages both the high efficiency of data-driven techniques and the convenient shape representation provided by active surfaces, which proves highly practical for incorporating a priori knowledge as well as for the post-analysis of segmented objects. By considering a complete 3D volume, our method ensures segmentation consistency across all three dimensions, unlike many approaches that handle volumes in a slice-by-slice manner. Additionally, it theoretically enables the representation of any object with spherical topology, overcoming the limitations of common 3D methods that rely on object convexity assumptions. Furthermore, the continuous representation of objects allows for a resolution-independent description, facilitating the extraction of various geometric features of interest (e.g., local curvature, principal deformations). We demonstrate both the quality of the segmentation produced by our method and the richness of the accessible geometric features through an extensive set of experiments conducted on multiple real and simulated datasets, including objects with challenging geometries.

articles.title: Enrich.AI: An Agentic AI Platform for Interactive GeneSet Enrichment Analysis and Biological Interpretation
articles.abstract: Motivation: Enrichment analysis is widely used to extract biological meanings from gene lists. However, the large number of available tools and reference libraries often make the interpretation of results challenging. Inexperienced users lack clear guidance on which datasets and terms are most relevant to their data, whereas experienced researchers must navigate large result sets and consult multiple resources to identify biologically relevant findings. Integrating AI into this process can help to bridge these gaps. Results: We present Enrich.AI, a conversational biology assistant that integrates statistical enrichment analysis with automated biological interpretation. The agent operates on an LLM-based ReAct architecture and dynamically selects among the tools for enrichment (220+ gene set libraries), literature search (40+ million publications via Europe PMC), gene annotation, and database retrieval. Given a gene list and a short description of the biological context, Enrich.AI produces a written interpretation grounded in the retrieved literature and six interactive, configurable visualizations. A conversational interface enables human-in-the-loop refinement, letting researchers without programming experience explore results iteratively. The reliability of these interpretations was validated through a systematic evaluation on 50 gene sets, demonstrating high faithfulness to retrieved evidence and a low hallucination rate.

articles.title: Eye movement markers of relational encoding predict scene memory precision
articles.abstract: Recalling scenes and events depends on how information is relationally organised in memory, but it is unclear whether the organisation of eye movements during encoding, rather than simply how much is explored, shapes what is remembered. Using a scene-viewing paradigm and drawing-based free recall task to capture the content and structure of remembered scenes, we examined whether scene memory was better explained by 'lower-order' measures reflecting the magnitude and spatial extent of sampling, or 'higher-order' measures capturing gaze organisation and temporal dynamics. Relative to lower-order measures (number of fixations and scanpath length), memory precision was better predicted by repeated sampling of viewed regions (refixations) and gaze distributions (stationary gaze entropy) during encoding. Thus, the organisation of visual attention, rather than sampling quantity, contributed to scene representations that preserved relationships between elements. These findings highlight a role for spatial gaze dynamics in optimally encoding organised, relational scene representations for episodic memory.

articles.title: Facial color properties affect perceived age.
articles.abstract: Age is a fundamental social attribute that affects rights, responsibilities and even social status. Color information of the face can affect perceived age, but the nature of its contribution, independent of luminance information, remains underexplored. To better characterize the role of color in age perception, we conducted two experiments. In our first experiment, we tested whether natural age-related changes in facial color alone can drive changes in perceived age. In our second experiment, we manipulated red-green contrast across faces aged 18-91 and tested the effect of this manipulation of perceived youthfulness. Our findings demonstrate that natural age-related color changes do provide cues for age perception, dissociable from luminance information. We also found that the optimal red-green contrast level to make faces look the youngest was significantly higher than the originals, meaning that faces tended to appear younger when their redness was accentuated, even though average face redness increases with age. Our analysis revealed that younger faces required greater increases in redness level compared to their older counterparts to achieve the youngest appearance. These results suggest that the spatial distribution of redness contributes to apparent youthfulness, especially in younger faces.

articles.title: First confirmed record in Melilla of Gerbillus campestris Loche, 1867 (Muridae: Gerbillinae) for Spain
articles.abstract: The fieldwork was carried out between December 2023 and June 2025, with the aim, among others, of confirming the possible presence of the North African Gerbil (Gerbillus campestris) in Melilla. To this end, 56 camera trap stations were installed, each equipped with a camera trap. Of the total number of camera trap stations installed, the presence of Gerbillus campestris was detected in six of them, representing a capture success rate of 10.71%. Following the detection of the species, a specimen was captured using cage traps. For identification purposes, samples of epithelial tissue from the ear and faeces were collected. These samples were sent to the Institute of Vertebrate Biology of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Brno, Czech Republic, for analysis. There, DNA was extracted from the samples using the Innu PREP DNA Mini Kit 2.0 (IST Innuscreen GmbH, Germany) according to the manufacturer's protocol. The results obtained confirm, for the first time through records of the species, the presence of Gerbillus campestris in Melilla and, therefore, in Spain and Europe.

articles.title: Forensic likelihood ratios for shotgun sequencing data from DNA mixtures
articles.abstract: Shotgun sequencing of DNA mixtures has the potential to become an important tool in forensic genetics, particularly for degraded samples or complex mixtures. However, the analysis of shotgun-sequenced mixtures is challenged by several confounding factors, including sequencing errors, population structure, the potential presence of relatives, linkage, and linkage disequilibrium. Additionally, the statistical methods currently available for such data are limited. Here, we develop likelihood ratios that summarize the evidence for the presence of a suspect's DNA in a mixture, assuming genotypes of the suspect and the victim are available, while accounting for DNA from unknown contributors modeled either as general population contamination or as a single contaminating individual. We show that these likelihood ratios are not robust to model assumptions and can falsely support the presence of the suspect's DNA when the true contributor is even a distant relative. We therefore propose a combined evidence score, $\Lambda$: the likelihood ratio minimized over contamination models, reported only when the evidence favors the suspect over a hypothesized sibling by at least a factor of C (default $C=10$) under at least one contamination model, and otherwise set to 1 (log $\Lambda$ = 0). In simulations based on 1000 Genomes data, $\Lambda$ retains nearly all power to detect true contributors at mixture proportions as low as 5\% while eliminating the false positives produced by model mis-specification, population structure, and by untested relatives. The methods are implemented in the open-source program DNAMIXTURE, providing the forensic and population genetics community a resource for robustly identifying small individual contributions to a DNA mixture. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. NIH, R35GM153400

articles.title: From Benchmark to Bench: Can Agents Survive Real-World Drug Discovery?
articles.abstract: Agentic systems increasingly coordinate molecular-design tools, but it is unclear which layer of the stack limits outcomes on real projects. We developed MAGI, an open modular agent that authors objectives, launches and monitors optimization, interprets structure activity relationships, and revises its strategy accordingly. MAGI generates molecules either directly through the LLM or by delegating to REINVENT4, with scoring services interchangeable behind a common contract. We tested it across nine retrospective lead-optimization campaigns from three pharmaceutical companies, replayed under fixed temporal cutoffs. Both routes produced valid structures: LLM proposals stayed closer to local chemistry and reached comparable or higher primary activity in fewer operations, whereas REINVENT explored broader chemical space. Whether a campaign met its objective depended on the predictive models, not on the generation route: attainment followed model accuracy on the chemistry proposed, dropping once that chemistry moved outside the model applicability domain. Separately, a blinded evaluation asked whether the MAGI output could pass as expert work: chemists were not able to discriminate agentic proposals from held-out compounds, and judged the SAR reasoning broadly plausible yet incomplete. Together, these results position MAGI as a coordination layer pluggable into existing computational chemistry workflows. The ceiling on real projects, however, remains currently set by scorer applicability rather than by tool orchestration.

articles.title: Gene transcriptional profiling to assess Chinook salmon osmoregulatory resilience to salinity challenges
articles.abstract: Given unprecedented environmental change, Pacific salmonids are becoming increasingly threatened; however, genomic technologies provide an opportunity to assess Pacific salmonid resilience to on-going environmental change. Also, given increasing conservation and animal welfare concerns, non-lethal tissue sampling is emerging for assessing the physiological status of wild species. Relatively few studies, however, have compared the transcriptomic response of fish sampled non-lethally versus lethally for fish health and stress quantification. Here, we conducted a comparative gene transcriptional profiling study using 28 qPCR assays on the OpenArray platform as an osmoregulatory stress transcriptional profiling chip. We sampled both non-lethal (gill biopsies, skin swabs, and water [eRNA]) and lethal (whole gill and liver) tissue samples from Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) smolts exposed for 0 h, 24 h, and 72 h to freshwater (0 PSU), brackish water (15 PSU) or seawater (30 PSU). We observed that most assays showed higher qPCR amplification success in both non-lethal gill biopsies and lethal gill tissues, compared to other tissues. We found more significant differences in transcript abundance in traditional lethal tissues compared to non-lethal tissues. With increasing duration of salinity exposure, gene transcript levels were typically upregulated in seawater samples compared to freshwater samples for both non-lethal and lethal tissues. The targeted genes for both non-lethal and lethal tissues were significantly and positively correlated across time points. Our findings support the use of non-lethal tissue sampling to improve Chinook salmon hatchery rearing, inform hatchery release timing, and facilitate future field application for the conservation of wild stocks.

articles.title: High-level visual and motor regions are doubly dissociated in controlled tasks but only at specific times during natural behaviors
articles.abstract: Our knowledge of the neural basis of sensory and motor information processing comes largely from recording brain activity in controlled settings. This approach, while insightful, blinds us from understanding natural behaviors, which involve far richer visual inputs and far larger range of movements. The prevailing belief is that, during natural behaviors, movement information would modulate visual cortex, and visual inputs would modulate motor cortex. Alternatively, this mixing might only reflect correlations between sensory inputs and movements present during natural behavior. To resolve this issue, we performed wireless recordings from high-level visual (IT) and motor regions (PMv/PFC) in freely moving monkeys while they performed a natural task and a fixation task. In each task, we extracted visual and movement features and asked to what degree these features explained neural activity. In the fixation task, we found a striking double dissociation whereby visual (but not movement) features predicted neural activity in IT, whereas motor (but not visual) features predicted neural activity in PMv & PFC. This dissociation was far weaker in the natural task but present particularly at key events when the visual and motor features were less correlated. Thus, high-level sensory and motor regions in the brain are doubly dissociated under controlled conditions, and remain so at specific times during natural behavior.

articles.title: Hormonal factors are poor indicators of endometriosis pain
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a common yet understudied condition in which sex hormones play a key role in the etiology and pathophysiology of the disease. Sex hormones are dysregulated in endometriosis and are pharmacologically targeted to reduce symptoms including pain, but the relationships between endometriosis-related pain with sex hormone levels and their receptors are not clear. In 60 women previously diagnosed or undergoing laparoscopic surgery for the diagnosis of endometriosis, we collected patient-reported endometriosis/pelvic pain intensity in the last 30 days, pain interference scale, and the Endometriosis Health Profile 30 (EHP30) pain subscale. In a sub-sample of 38 participants, biopsies from control non-lesion pelvic peritoneum and endometrial lesion tissues were collected during surgery to analyze the tissue abundance of the primary receptors for estrogen, as well as androgen, progesterone, and prolactin receptors. Serum was collected to analyze systemic sex hormone levels including estradiol, prolactin, progesterone, and testosterone. Between tissues, we found elevated transcript levels for estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) in lesions, but no difference in estrogen receptor beta (ESR2) transcript levels between tissue samples were found. Relating tissue receptor transcript levels to clinical pain revealed that only ESR1 and PGR in lesions were negatively associated with endometriosis/pelvic pain intensity, however, following false discovery rate correction the association with ESR1 was no longer statistically significant. No other tissue or systemic factors were associated with clinical pain outcomes. Together, these data demonstrate unique alterations in receptor abundance in lesions yet select transcript levels only weakly relate to pain in endometriosis.

articles.title: IgG4 antibody repertoire diversity is stable over several years in health and autoimmune disease
articles.abstract: Despite its relative anti-inflammatory nature, IgG4 is involved in a variety of pathological conditions such as autoimmune disease and cancer. To investigate whether the IgG4 repertoire presents any abnormalities in diseases where IgG4 autoantibodies predominate, we charted longitudinal IgG4 repertoires in health, in an IgG4-mediated autoimmune disease (AID; muscle-specific kinase myasthenia gravis (MuSK MG)), and in IgG1/IgG3 mediated AIDs (acetylcholine receptor (AChR) MG and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS). In total, we assessed 218 samples of 69 donors using mass spectrometry-based antibody repertoire analysis, covering a timespan of up to eight years. Despite being superficially inconspicuous in clonal diversity and abundances, we detected a slightly elevated number of IgG4 clones in MuSK MG patients compared to healthy donors. Notably, this observation did not coincide with drastic repertoire changes during treatment, suggesting that a large portion of the IgG4 repertoire is not significantly affected by common MuSK MG treatment regimens. Comparing the IgG4 antibody repertoires of all donors, we found that they were exceptionally unique for each individual. Against what would be expected in the case of a constantly adapting antibody repertoire, a large portion of the IgG4 clones remained stable without any further maturation. This observation even extended to patients receiving B cell depleting or IgG modulating treatments. Our findings suggest that a dominating fraction of the IgG4 pool may be produced by long-lived plasma cells, which are unaffected by disease or medical interventions. ### Competing Interest Statement MGH and JV are coinventors on patent applications based on MuSK-related research. The LUMC receives royalties from IBL and Argenx, MGH and JV receive royalties from Argenx. AJRH is co-founder of Abvion. All other authors report no disclosures. articles.title: Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomes identifies neuronal heat-stress-associated candidate genes in a reef-building coral
articles.abstract: Cell-type-specific molecular responses are obscured in bulk RNA sequencing, whereas generating matched single-cell datasets across environmental conditions remains costly and technically challenging, particularly in non-model organisms. Here, we present a workflow that integrates existing bulk and single-cell RNA-seq resources to prioritize cell-type-associated environmental-response genes. We demonstrate the workflow by examining heat-stress-associated neuronal genes in the reef-building coral Stylophora pistillata. Neuronal genes were first identified based on cell type-specific expression in single-cell transcriptomic data and then intersected with differentially expressed genes from bulk RNA-seq datasets under heat-stress. In parallel, we applied a deconvolution approach to infer cell type-specific expression changes directly from bulk data, independently capturing neuronal transcriptional responses. This integrated pipeline reduced thousands of heat-responsive genes previously identified in bulk RNA-seq studies to nine heat-associated, neuron-enriched candidates. Eight of the nine candidates showed their highest mean expression in the same neuronal subcluster. Targeted sequence-based characterization supported the identification of a TRPA-family ion channel, two calmodulin/centrin-family Ca2+-binding proteins, and a Class A/rhodopsin-like GPCR of unresolved ligand specificity. Two additional candidates were predicted secreted proteins belonging to conserved coral protein families, while the molecular functions of the remaining candidates remained unresolved. Their coordinated regulation suggests heat-associated remodeling of neuronal sensory and intracellular signaling processes. Our workflow provides a scalable framework for extracting cell type-associated molecular responses from existing transcriptomic resources and prioritizing candidates for further investigation. More broadly, it offers a generalizable strategy for investigating cell type-specific gene expression responses across organisms, cell types, and environmental conditions without requiring new single-cell datasets.

articles.title: Inverse relationship between mitochondrial and non-coding nuclear DNA content in free-living kinetoplastids
articles.abstract: The evolution of genome size and eukaryotic genome organisation has puzzled evolutionary biologists for decades. Are differences in DNA content and protein-coding capacity of eukaryotic genomes a result of natural selection, or neutral processes? If they were shaped by natural selection, which features might be connected with these differences: cell volume, ecological strategy, availability of nutrients, etc.? Kinetoplastids are protists with compact nuclear genomes that almost entirely lack introns, but whose mitochondrial DNA content (kDNA) can rival that of their nuclei. We hypothesised that the reduction in non-protein coding nuclear DNA content during the evolution of kinetoplastids is connected with an increase in kDNA content: species with larger fractions of total cellular DNA that is allocated to kDNA will have concomitantly smaller fractions of non-coding DNA in the nuclear genome. We developed a framework for estimation of DNA content in both the mitochondria and nuclei from quantitative fluorescence microscopy data, and inferred the fraction of non-coding DNA in nuclear genomes based on the combination of transcriptomic and fluorescence imaging data. Across 10 genetically distant isolates from diverse free-living kinetoplastid lineages, there is indeed a trend towards a lower proportion of non-protein-coding nuclear DNA when kDNA proportion is higher relative to the total DNA in the cell. This observation is consistent with the hypothesis that in free-living kinetoplastids, mitochondrial and nuclear genomes might co-evolve in terms of their DNA content. This finding raises the possibility that natural selection acts on genome size evolution in kinetoplastids, and contributes evidence and methodology to address this question more broadly in eukaryotes.

articles.title: Joining Two Perspectives of the Proteome with the Trypsin+HTA Protease Workflow
articles.abstract: Proteolysis can be completed in a single-step, rapid (5-30 minutes) reaction using hyperthermoacidic archaeal (HTA) proteases. Protocol simplicity and stability of HTA proteases in ambient storage conditions removes many logistical barriers to widespread deployment of proteomic analysis. HTA protease cleavage selectivity is complicated but quantitatively reproducible and generates peptides that negligibly overlap with trypsin. Tryptic and HTA protease peptides emphasize different proteins and provide complementary coverage of amino acid sequence and post-translational modification (PTM) sites. Digestion of a sample's separate aliquot with HTA protease is a minor addition to trypsin-based workflows, but LC-MS analysis of both sets of peptides is not practical for large cohorts. This manuscript evaluates the identifications and reproducibility of LC-MS analysis of tryptic and HTA protease peptide mixtures. Adding HTA protease peptides to 20% increased total protein identifications by 24% on average in neat plasma and identified 216 additional non-artifact modifications compared to conventional trypsin-only bottom-up proteomic analysis. This approach is reproducible and does not increase sample preparation or analysis time. Peptides from each protease present independent opportunities to quantify overlapping proteins and a quantification model was developed in which the protease with the most complete data is selected for each protein while the second protease is used to infer missing values. This cross-protease inference is more accurate than the alternative minimum, mean, or nearest neighbor imputations. Finally, biomarkers discovered through HTA protease peptides are amenable to rapid HTA protease only proteomic workflows thus streamlining translation from discovery to fieldable applications.

articles.title: Macrophages from Holstein and Normande cows respond differently to Escherichia coli and Streptococcus uberis
articles.abstract: Macrophages, alongside mammary epithelial cells, are major contributors to the innate immune response triggered by bacterial invasion of the mammary gland. To investigate breed-specific immune mechanisms, we stimulated monocyte-derived macrophages from Holstein and Normande cattle with Escherichia coli and Streptococcus uberis, two major mastitis pathogens. We monitored bacterial survival using [méthode] and profiled gene expression via RNA-seq. E. coli exhibited significantly higher survival 6 hours post-infection compared to S. uberis (p < 0.05). Moreover, E. coli induced a robust transcriptional response, with 4403 differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1), versus only 813 for S. uberis. Qualitative differences were also observed: genes such as CCL2 and CSF1 were uniquely induced by S. uberis. Additionally, macrophages from Holstein and Normande cattle showed distinct expression profiles: 185, 45, and 174 genes were differentially expressed at steady state or after E. coli or S. uberis stimulation, respectively. These genes were enriched in immune-related pathways. Overall, our results demonstrate a stronger response to E. coli, although S. uberis specifically induces a subset of genes. The observed breed-specific differences may reflect underlying immune mechanisms that could influence disease susceptibility, warranting further functional validation.

articles.title: Molecular anatomy of the glomerular filtration barrier reveals topology-encoded albumin sieving
articles.abstract: The kidney filters plasma rapidly while retaining albumin, yet where and how this selectivity is encoded within the glomerular filtration barrier remain unresolved. Here we combine cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) of vitrified mouse glomeruli with structure-resolved transport modelling to predict albumin passage from the native three-dimensional architecture of the barrier. Among the three barrier layers, endothelial fenestrae and the flexible Nephrin-Neph1 slit-diaphragm lattice are substantially permeable to albumin. The glomerular basement membrane (GBM) instead provides the dominant restriction through steric exclusion governed by void-network topology. In local GBM reconstructions, water traverses broadly connected void space, whereas narrow throats exclude albumin, leaving few accessible paths. To scale this mechanism to the tissue level, we combine structural statistics from local cryo-ET volumes with mesoscale measurements of GBM heterogeneity to generate representative ensembles. Integrating these ensembles with other layers predicts whole-barrier albumin sieving in close agreement with an independent measurement. The topology-driven mechanism also explains early filtration failure in Alport syndrome mice, in which collagen-IV disruption remodels the GBM network and opens albumin-accessible paths while cellular interfaces remain preserved. These findings identify the structural origin of glomerular albumin selectivity and establish a quantitative route from locally resolved architecture to tissue-scale physiology.

articles.title: Netrin signaling shapes sexually dimorphic neurite branching of a sex-shared interneuron in C. elegans
articles.abstract: Sexually dimorphic behaviors arise from underlying differences in neural circuit architecture between the sexes, yet the molecular mechanisms that establish these structural differences remain poorly understood. In Caenorhabditis elegans , the sex-shared interneuron AVG exhibits sexually dimorphic synaptic connectivity, offering a model for investigating the development of sexually dimorphic neuronal morphology. Here, we identified that AVG displays male-specific neurite branching and demonstrated that the conserved axon guidance cue UNC-6/Netrin and its receptor UNC-40/DCC are essential for this structural remodeling. Cell-specific manipulation of sexual identity revealed that male identity confers branching competence to AVG. Loss of UNC-6 or UNC-40 abolished branch formation, whereas loss of the alternate Netrin receptor UNC-5/Unc5 had no detectable effect. Cell-specific rescue experiments showed that UNC-40 functions in AVG through its UNC-6 binding domains. Furthermore, genetic ablation of the male-specific presynaptic neuron PCA, which expresses unc-6, diminished AVG branch length, establishing PCA as a candidate local source of UNC-6. Together, our findings support a model in which presynaptic UNC-6/Netrin cues from male-specific neurons promote dimorphic neurite branching in sex-shared neurons, illustrating how evolutionarily conserved signaling molecules are redeployed during sexual maturation to sculpt sex-specific neural circuits.

articles.title: Nutrient-sensitive histone propionylation regulates T cell fate and function
articles.abstract: Tissue microenvironments differ widely in nutrient composition; yet how local nutrient conditions shape epigenetic programs that direct immune cell fate is poorly understood. We identify histone lysine propionylation (Kpr) as a chromatin mechanism linking nutrient availability to T cell fate decisions. Proteomic analysis reveals that Kpr is broadly reduced in exhausted T cells. H3K18pr is enriched at stemness-associated loci in effector T cells and depleted upon exhaustion. Isoleucine and propionate supply propionyl-CoA in T cells, and restricted nutrient availability within the tumor microenvironment limits histone Kpr, promoting T cell exhaustion. Disrupting isoleucine catabolism in T cells further suppresses Kpr, without altering histone acetylation, and impairs T cell function and antitumor immunity in a manner rescued by propionate. Dietary supplementation of isoleucine and propionate increases Kpr in tumor infiltrating lymphocytes, limits exhaustion, and improves tumor control. These findings establish a microenvironment-chromatin axis crucial for antitumor immunity and amenable to nutritional intervention.

articles.title: On-demand surround suppression explains the spatiotemporal window of the tilt illusion
articles.abstract: What we see at one location depends on what surrounds it. Such contextual e[ff]ects are thought to arise from neural signals that travel across the retinotopic representations.Because these signals need more time to travel longer distances, a more distant surround should influence perception most strongly when presented earlier, compensating for its delay. We tested this prediction in human observers using a visual illusion in which a central target appears tilted away from the orientation of its surround (tilt illusion). Measuring the temporal window of this illusion using psychophysical reverse correlation revealed the opposite: the most e[ff]ective surround occurred progressively later as distance increased. Computational modelling demonstrated that this reversal is explained if the visual system sends out a query that recruits contextual information on demand. Perceptual appearance may thus be constructed through temporally unfolding interactions in which context is actively gathered, not passively received.

articles.title: Overexpressing FLP Recombinase Can Cause Synaptic Trafficking Defects in C. elegans
articles.abstract: Site-specific recombinases, such as Cre recombinase (Cre) and FLP recombinase (FLPase), are popular tools that enable precise spatiotemporal control over fluorescent reporter genes. However, studies show that increased Cre expression can lead to cytotoxic phenotypes including DNA damage, cell cycle arrest, cell death, and aneuploidy. In contrast, there is little-to-no known cytotoxicity associated with FLPase. FLPase is considered to be the safer, if less efficient, recombinase. To compensate for decreased efficiency, researchers will often increase expression of the FLPase to ensure a complete gene edit. Despite previous evidence that FLPase is nontoxic at high doses, we report that high expression of FLPase from multi-copy extrachromosomal arrays can disrupt synaptic protein trafficking in C. elegans . We discovered several off-target effects of high FLPase expression including mislocalization of the pre-synaptic marker FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and decreased synaptic abundance, transport, and expression of the ionotropic glutamate receptor subunit GLR-1. Neither overexpression of an inactive FLPase, low activity FLPase, nor mCherry under the same promoter elicited these effects. However, single-copy expression of the FLPase construct reliably tags FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and does not lead to these off-target effects. This work supports growing awareness that tyrosine recombinases can become cytotoxic at high doses.

articles.title: Pathological tau leads to network hyperexcitability through neuronal-subtype-specific functional impairment
articles.abstract: Pathological tau disrupts neuronal activity and brain function in Alzheimer s disease and other tauopathies. However, the underlying mechanisms for neuronal network dysfunction remain largely unknown. Using human inducible pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) - derived neurons, we show that the familial MAPT P301L mutation leads to neuronal network hyperexcitability. Imbalanced excitation and inhibition were attributable to neuronal subtype-specific tau pathology that was associated with different alterations of tau interactomes in excitatory versus inhibitory neurons. Suppressing enhanced excitatory synaptic transmission or blocking Ca2+ influx resulting from enhanced P301L tau/AHNAK interaction in inhibitory neurons rescued the neuronal network hyperexcitability. This study expands our understanding on how disease-causing tau mutations alter the excitatory/inhibitory balance, leading to network dysfunction in human neurons.

articles.title: Polyphyletic origin and horizontal exchange drive the emergence of a novel resistance-breaking Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lactucae race
articles.abstract: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lactucae (Fola), the cause of lettuce fusarium wilt, poses an increasing threat to global production due to the rapid emergence of resistance breaking isolates. However, the evolutionary origins and mechanisms underpinning this diversification remain poorly understood. We characterised 103 Fola isolates using molecular profiling, selecting ten key isolates for long-read whole-genome sequencing and performed in planta virulence assays for selected isolates. This included the first assemblies for Fola2 and Fola3, recent resistance-breaking variants and a highly divergent isolate from France designated as a putative novel race, FolaX. Phylogenomic analysis revealed that Fola is polyphyletic, with lettuce pathogenicity acquired independently across divergent F. oxysporum clades. Despite this, all lineages share a conserved "PanFola" effector set with near-identical sequences, indicating extensive horizontal gene transfer. Resistance-breaking Fola variants within established races were linked to copy number variations and targeted deletions, such as the loss of the SIX8/PSE1 locus in Fola4+. Conversely, FolaX possessed a divergent core genome and a chimeric accessory genome derived from multiple Fola lineages via segmental chromosome transfer and transposon-mediated reshuffling. Our findings highlight the remarkable evolutionary plasticity of Fola and the need for breeding strategies that address the dynamic nature of effector repertoires.

articles.title: QTL analysis of essential oil, seed shattering, thousand-grain weight and stalk attachment rate in Carum carvi
articles.abstract: Caraway (Carum carvi L., 2n = 2x = 20) is a medicinal and aromatic plant of the Apiaceae family valued for its essential oil with the major terpenoids carvone and limonene. While the essential oil content represents an important quality trait, low seed shattering and high thousand-grain weight (TGW) are key determinants of seed yield. As molecular tools remain scarce within Apiaceae breeding beyond carrot, we conducted a QTL mapping for these seed-related traits using two previously established F2 populations (Effective N(P1) = 236; N(P2) = 266). In P1 with the non-shattering maternal parent Rekord, QTL mapping revealed at least one shattering locus on LG03 (PVE: 9.9%). In addition, loci associated with essential oil (LG08, 10.5% PVE) and TGW (LG09, 11.1% PVE) were detected. In P2, we identified six essential-oil loci (LG02-06, LG10; combined PVE: 49.2%), with five loci affecting both carvone and limonene, and one (LG03) exclusively limonene. Additionally, a major QTL for TGW mapped to LG02 (PVE: 15.6%). For stalk attachment rate one minor QTL was detected (LG07, 8.5% PVE), while no QTL co-localized with the major shattering locus. To pave the path towards fine-mapping, we designed and validated 26 diagnostic PACE markers covering five key QTLs.

articles.title: Quantitative MRI-based assessment of the ultrastructural compactness of myelin lamellae
articles.abstract: Efficient neuronal communication relying on rapid saltatory conduction depends not only on the amount of myelin wrapping axons but also on myelin compact organisation. Yet, current quantitative MRI myelin imaging methods, such as Myelin Water Imaging (MWI) and quantitative Magnetization Transfer (qMT), are designed to estimate myelin content and are often treated as interchangeable, overlooking myelin organisation. We introduce Structural Myelin Integrity (SMI), a quantitative MRI metric designed to distinguish myelin compact organisation from content. SMI combines the distinct biophysical sensitivities of MWI and qMT to separate the water confined between myelin layers from the total myelin membrane mass. We evaluated SMI in two rodent models of myelin decompaction and one remyelination model, validating our findings with synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering and electron microscopy. SMI detected myelin layers decompaction despite largely preserved myelin membranes, revealing structural abnormalities that were not explained by myelin content alone. During remyelination, SMI returned closer to healthy values at early timepoints than myelin-content metrics, consistent with the formation of thin-but-compact sheaths. These findings indicate that myelin content and organisation can dissociate and establish SMI as a non-invasive marker of myelin organisation, compatible with existing clinical MRI approaches for studying white matter changes not detected today.

articles.title: Quercetin alters redox homeostasis, induces MAPK activation and promotes DNA damage in vGPCR-transformed endothelial cells
articles.abstract: Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is an angioproliferative tumor associated with infection by human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), also known as Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Among the viral genes involved in KS pathogenesis, the viral G protein-coupled receptor (vGPCR) plays a key role in oncogenic transformation and angiogenesis, and its sustained activity contributes to tumor development and maintenance. Quercetin (QUE), a naturally occurring flavonoid with well-recognized anticancer properties, has been shown to reduce cell viability and proliferation and to induce apoptosis in vGPCR-transformed endothelial cells. This study further investigated the mechanisms underlying the antineoplastic effects of QUE in vGPCR cells, an in vitro model of Kaposi's sarcoma. Initially, QUE promoted the activation of MAPK signaling pathways in vGPCR cells, increasing the phosphorylation levels of ERK1/2, JNK1/2, and p38, without affecting AKT phosphorylation. In parallel, QUE increased intracellular oxidant levels, followed by lipid peroxidation and DNA damage, supporting a link between oxidative imbalance and genotoxicity. However, increased total glutathione content, and unaltered Gpx4 mRNA expression, suggest the induction of oxidative stress and compensatory antioxidant responses. Furthermore, increased intracellular oxidant levels were associated with MAPK signaling activation, particularly JNK1/2, whereas ERK1/2 and p38 activation may reflect a compensatory response that is insufficient to overcome QUE-induced cytotoxicity. Taken together, these findings indicate that QUE exerts antiproliferative effects in vGPCR cells through a mechanism involving oxidative stress, MAPK activation, and DNA damage, supporting its potential relevance in the study of therapeutic strategies for virus-associated malignancies.

articles.title: Refining Protein Co-Membership in Reactome: A Weighted Scoring Approach Based on Hierarchy and Sequences of Patwhays
articles.abstract: In network biology, analyzing pathways is critical to study mechanisms or sequences of biological events. The pathway co-membership approach aims to link proteins belonging to the same pathway inside a network that is a clique. Although this method is great for projecting pathway knowledge onto proteins, it remains unsuitable for some downstream applications relying on graph distances like random walks with restart. To address this limitation, we introduce a weighted pathway co-membership method that incorporates biological distances between proteins. We achieve this by developing an abstraction framework for Reactome pathways, which captures both their hierarchical organization and sequential relationships. By assigning weights to these abstractions, we define a scoring system for proteins within the pathway co-membership clique. We illustrate our approach using a Reactome pathway ("Signaling by TGF-beta receptor complex", R-HSA-170834), and explain how we generate the weighted co-membership cliques of the 29 Reactome top-level pathways. Next, we construct the entire weighted pathway co membership network of the Reactome knowledge base. Validation and evaluation of our method is performed using cancer hallmark gene sets and a random walk with restart experiment, comparing our approach to state-of-the-art methods. We show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods for gene prioritization on cancer hallmarks.

articles.title: Resolution-aware spectral parameterization reveals robust context-dependent aperiodic EEG dynamics during real-world table tennis
articles.abstract: Mobile EEG can link neuroimaging to natural behavior, but effects recorded during movement, and sport in particular, are difficult to interpret because neural activity overlaps with signals from movement, muscle activity, and cable movement artifacts. We analyzed the OpenNeuro Real World Table Tennis dataset to test whether peri-hit spectral activity could be analyzed and how it differed between human-opponent and ball-machine play. Data from 25 participants comprising EEG, noise-layers, EMG and motion recordings was analyzed with pre-hit, impact, and post-hit windows. EEG power bands were residualized using trial-level root mean square from noise-layer, EMG, and motion/miscellaneous channels. Spectral parameterization modeled spectra as an aperiodic component plus periodic peaks. The principal short-window model was resolution-aware; sensitivity analyses reduced model complexity, used a 2.0-s peri-hit subwindow (-1.0 to +1.0 s), or disabled periodic fitting. Results showed residualized alpha and beta power was lower during ball-machine play, including pre-hit posterior alpha power. The clearest context difference was a higher ball-machine aperiodic exponent over posterior and parietal sensors, corresponding to a steeper broadband spectral slope. Posterior post-hit means were 0.451 and 0.606 for human-opponent and ball-machine play, respectively. A focal parietal effect persisted across specifications. The results support artifact-informed, resolution-aware spectral analysis as an effective approach for detecting robust spectral differences between naturalistic visuomotor contexts and suggest that EEG may provide useful information about the processes engaged by different practice environments, without establishing a single cognitive or physiological mechanism or demonstrating a training outcome.

articles.title: SAIL: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Alignment of Human Vision and Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.abstract: Alignment between human high-level visual representations and those of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a quantitative framework for understanding information processing in human vision. However, similarities between model and brain representations do not directly reveal the semantic content underlying their correspondence, as this content is difficult to isolate in entangled MLLM representations. Here, we introduce SAIL, an interpretable framework that formulates voxel interpretation as a multi-unit sparse semantic correspondence problem between MLLMs and human vision. First, we train unified cross-layer sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on MLLM representations of Natural Scenes Dataset images and captions, and align each brain voxel with multiple SAE units. Second, we quantify semantic similarity between their top-response image sets to map semantic alignment across the cortex. We project multiple semantic labels back onto the cortex to interpret the content of this alignment. Finally, we assess these correspondences using category responses measured in independent fLoc experiments. Compared with SAEs trained independently at each layer, SAIL exhibits lower redundancy in SAE unit response profiles and higher semantic alignment. We find that semantic alignment is organized along the human ventral visual pathway across the models and subjects examined. The projected labels reveal semantic preferences within canonical visual regions, while fLoc experiments show agreement between predicted and measured category response patterns. Exploratory analyses further reveal cortical distributions of action-related semantics consistent with established functional accounts of lateral occipitotemporal and posterior parietal cortex. Overall, SAIL provides an interpretable account of the semantic correspondences between MLLM representations and human visual responses.

articles.title: Sex hormones gate the neuronal control of dendritic cell migration and immunity
articles.abstract: How endocrine states modulate local immune responses is a fundamental question in immunology. Sexual dimorphism is a striking example: females generally mount stronger immune responses than males, yet how sex hormones intersect with local signals is poorly understood. Here, we identify an endocrine-neuro-immune circuit in which sex hormones determine whether immune cells respond to nociceptor signals. In female skin, nociceptor-derived CGRP promotes dendritic cell (DC) migration and T cell priming indirectly through inflammatory monocytes. CGRP induces monocyte production of Activin A, which upregulates CXCR4 on DCs and promotes migration to draining lymph nodes. In males, androgen receptor signaling suppresses monocyte Activin A and silences this circuit. Disrupting the relay abolishes enhanced female immunity, whereas deleting androgen receptor in male monocytes restores neuronal control. Thus, sex hormones regulate immunity by determining how immune cells interpret neuronal signals, revealing how endocrine state can gate local neuroimmune communication to generate sex-specific immune responses.

articles.title: Sustained exposure to high dietary ethanol impairs bumblebee survival and locomotor performance
articles.abstract: Ethanol occurs naturally in sugar-rich foods used by insects, but its effects in bees have been studied primarily in honeybees. We tested whether dietary ethanol affects survival and locomotor performance in workers of the bumblebee Bombus terrestris (L.). In the survival experiment, workers were fed ethanol (0, 1, or 10%) for 21 days; in the locomotor experiment, they were fed the same doses for one or seven days, after which we measured spontaneous movement using an open-field assay. We measured the proportion of time in movement, speed of movement, path meander (curviness), and arena exploration. The 10% ethanol concentration greatly increased the risk of mortality, whereas the estimated effect of 1% ethanol was smaller and statistically inconclusive. In terms of locomotion, the largest differences occurred after seven days of exposure to 10% ethanol. Workers in this treatment showed greater path meander and lower exploration than control workers. Speed was also lowest in this group. Evidence that exposure for seven days was worse than for one day at the same concentration was detected only for exploration. No clear locomotor effect was detected at 1% ethanol exposure. These findings provide comparative data on sustained ethanol exposure in bumblebees and show a strong concentration-dependent contrast, with substantial effects under high-concentration challenge but no clear effects on the measured endpoints at 1%.

articles.title: The Gαi/o GPCR LPAR2 Acts as a Non-Classical Factor for Aldosterone Induced Injury in a Cardiomyocyte Model
articles.abstract: Aldosterone is a key regulator of systemic sodium, potassium, and fluid homeostasis. Chronic elevation of aldosterone, as observed in primary aldosteronism, chronic heart and kidney diseases, promotes cardiac hypertrophy, inflammation, fibrosis, and heart failure, which are further enhanced in aging. Although these pathological effects are primarily attributed to the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), emerging evidence suggests roles for nonclassical G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling. We identified lysophosphatidic acid receptor 2 (LPAR2) as a novel GPCR candidate that mediates aldosterone signaling in cardiomyocytes. Using AC16 human cardiomyocyte cells and reporter gene assays, we demonstrate that aldosterone activates a Gαi/o-dependent GPCR pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of LPAR2 internalization confirms its specific reaction to aldosterone. Functional studies revealed that aldosterone-induced cardiomyocyte injury requires both MR and LPAR2, where specific antagonists to both receptors reduced the ability of aldosterone to induce collagen expression and cell death markers. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized non-classical mechanism of aldosterone action in the heart and highlight LPAR2 as a promising therapeutic target for aldosterone-driven cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: The potato cyst nematode Globodera pallida possesses an expanded serotonergic nervous system
articles.abstract: The neurotransmitter serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) controls behaviours that are essential for the parasitic lifestyle of plant parasitic nematodes (PPNs). Here, we used serotonin immunochemistry and in situ hybridization for the serotonin synthesis genes, Gpa-tph-1 and Gpa-bas-1, to map its signalling pathways in Globodera pallida J2 infective stages. We identified fourteen serotonin-immunoreactive cell bodies around the pharyngeal median bulb and revealed that eleven of them co-express Gpa-tph-1 and Gpa-bas-1, confirming these are serotonin-synthesising neurons. Serotonin immunoreactivity was also localised in structures consistent with labelling of amphids, and in sixteen non-neuronal cells located in the middle and posterior region of the nematode. Depletion of serotonin with reserpine reduced the serotonin immunoreactivity in all fourteen cell bodies confirming their neuronal identity, but not in non-neuronal tissue. We identified additional, but infrequent expression of Gpa-tph-1 in two cells and expression of Gpa-bas-1 in one pair of symmetrically bilateral cells anterior to the median bulb, that lacked serotonin immunoreactivity. The results reveal distinct pools of serotonin distribution in G. pallida and indicate serotonin signalling is more complex than in other parasitic nematodes and C. elegans, highlighting evolutionary divergence in neurotransmitter identity.

articles.title: Tracing the dynamic recruitment trajectory of Optineurin between the centrosome and other macromolecular assemblies, signifying its role in cell cycle progression
articles.abstract: Spatiotemporal allocation and dynamic redistribution of centrosomal proteins are critical for coordinating the structural and molecular events that ensure successful cell division. While depletion of the multifunctional protein Optineurin (OPTN) impairs cell-cycle progression, our previous report of the presence of OPTN at key cell-division assemblies raised the question of how its trafficking is coordinated during cell division. In this study, using cell-cycle synchronisation coupled with flow cytometric analysis and confocal microscopy, we report that OPTN progressively dissociates from centrosomes during mitosis, redistributes to cytokinetic structures, accumulates at the spindle midzone, and then concentrates at the midbody during cytokinesis. Moreover, following this transition, OPTN progressively re-emerges at centrosomes during G1 of the subsequent cell cycle. Further, microtubule perturbation and regrowth assays provide evidence that OPTN recruitment and retention at the pericentriolar matrix (PCM) can occur independently of microtubules, whereas its exit is microtubule-dependent. Collectively, this study depicts, for the first time, a detailed movement trail of OPTN, highlighting its centrosome-linked redistribution and microtubule dependency. This context-dependent localisation and trafficking of OPTN across the centrosome-midbody axis establish a definitive spatiotemporal roadmap that can be strategically utilised to study its functional role in cell division.

articles.title: Tractable and Thermodynamically Consistent pKa Prediction via First-Dissociation Aggregation
articles.abstract: Ionization governs molecular behavior, yet predicting aqueous pKa accurately and tractably remains a fundamental challenge. Rigorous ensemble methods require enumerating a protonation-state space that grows exponentially with the number of ionizable sites, while fast graph predictors return numbers without thermodynamic consistency. Here we derive an exact thermodynamic identity showing that the macroscopic first-dissociation constant is fully determined by protonated-microstate populations and unique first-deprotonation events, eliminating the deprotonated ensemble algebraically and reducing aggregation to O(n+E) operations. We implement this identity in DTi-pKa, a dual-head graph neural network whose free-energy and dissociation heads are coupled by thermodynamic constraints. On four external benchmarks (355 molecules), DTi-pKa achieves a pooled MAE of 0.5665 pKa units, with 0.6285 on the 169 records lacking training-cache matches, while providing site-resolved micro-pKa values and protonation-state populations. Controlled ablations show that constraint placement at the level of the reported macroscopic equilibrium matters more than microscopic label precision--a design principle transferable to physics-informed machine learning beyond chemistry.
